meta.intro: Today's throughline: AI costs are falling at the model layer while capital chases the hardware and infrastructure underneath — and Japan is still building the on-ramps.
meta.briefingTitle: Haiku 5.5 Drops to $0.10, a16z Backs a 19-Year-Old's Agent PC, Cerebras Slides, and Rapidus Seeks Its First Customer
meta.summary: Inference is getting cheaper at the top of the stack while the money moves to the physical layer. Anthropic cut its small-model price 90%, even as Cerebras fell below its IPO price on a claim that OpenAI's fastest tier runs on Nvidia. Early money is backing local agent hardware (Ghost, a16z) and open agent harnesses (Nous at $1.5B). In Japan, the pattern is infrastructure without customers yet: Rapidus has 17 design partners and no named 2nm order, Fujitsu's agents wait until mid-2027, and seed rounds stay near $1M.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged — Sakana's Fugu orchestrates others' models rather than pretraining, and Anthropic's 90% Haiku price cut widens the cost gap Japanese labs must close.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Unchanged — DriveX's ~$1.15M seed and estie's ~¥16.6B listing sit beside US rounds like Nous at $1.5B and Ghost's a16z-led seed.

gaps.label: Domestic humanoid/robotics ownership
gaps.note: Unchanged — no new Japan robotics evidence today; Fujitsu's retail agents are software-only and slow, with GA in June 2027.

gaps.label: Domestic sovereign compute capacity
gaps.note: Down 1 — Rapidus has 17 design partners but no named 2nm customer, while US neoclouds raise hundreds of millions to add GPUs.

items.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 Cuts Anthropic's Cheapest Tier to $0.10/$0.50 per Million Tokens, a 90% List-Price Drop
items.dek: The third Claude 5.5 model undercuts OpenAI's small GPT-6 Luna on price and, per Anthropic, on OSWorld and Terminal-Bench.

analysis.happening: Released Oct 7 at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens under 100K-token prompts (Haiku 4.5 was $1/$5). Anthropic reports 72.4% on an OSWorld 2.1 subset and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ahead of GPT-6 Luna. First Haiku with an effort setting.
analysis.now: Sub-dollar agent loops become viable: routers, sub-agents and computer-use workers now cost almost nothing. Caveat: benchmarks are vendor-reported, and cyber/pentest use is restricted.
analysis.future: Watch OpenAI and Google price responses and third-party reproductions of the OSWorld number. Builders: re-run the cost model for multi-agent pipelines at roughly 10x cheaper small-model inference.

items.headline: Ghost, Founded by a 19-Year-Old, Raises $11M Seed Led by a16z for a $3,499 Screenless PC That Runs AI Agents Locally
items.dek: A hardware bet that the personal-agent box is a product category, with preorders open and shipping planned for late October.

analysis.happening: San Francisco's Ghost came out of stealth with an $11M seed led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Abstract, Audacious Ventures, SV Angel and Nova. Its Core machine packs an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU and is run by phone app or voice. Founder Zain Javaid is 19.
analysis.now: a16z is betting agents want always-on, private, local compute rather than cloud-only. Caveats: the 'sold out in hours' claim comes from one secondary source, one aggregator mislabels it a Series A, and $11M is small for hardware.
analysis.future: Watch late-October shipments and reviews, and whether Apple or Nvidia answer. The opening for builders is software and apps for local-agent boxes.

items.headline: Cerebras Hits a Post-IPO Low After SemiAnalysis Says OpenAI's Ultrafast Tier Runs on Nvidia, Just as Lockups Expire
items.dek: One unconfirmed workload claim plus insider unlocks cut about 20% off the newest public AI-chip pure play in a week.

analysis.happening: SemiAnalysis said OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast tier (~300 tokens/sec) runs on Nvidia GPUs. CBRS closed at $166.43 on Oct 2, below its $185 IPO price, as up to 19.4M shares (8% of shares outstanding) unlocked. Altman called Cerebras a close partner; the stock bounced about 9% Oct 5.
analysis.now: It shows how fragile a one-customer inference-chip story is, and how fast Nvidia can answer on speed. Caveat: the claim is SemiAnalysis's inference, not confirmed by OpenAI.
analysis.future: More unlocks reportedly land Oct 14 and Oct 28 (dates vary by source). Watch Cerebras's first earnings and any OpenAI disclosure on Ultrafast hardware.

items.headline: Nous Research Books $90M at $1.5B to Sell Its MIT-Licensed Hermes Agent to Companies
items.dek: An open-source agent harness with 214k GitHub stars is trying to turn self-hosting popularity into per-seat revenue.

analysis.happening: Nous announced a $90M Series B at $1.5B (Robot Ventures led; Nvidia, USV and Menlo reported) plus Hermes Business and Enterprise tiers. Hosted plans run $20-200/month. Company-reported: about $36M annualized revenue in mid-September, $100M targeted by year end.
analysis.now: Open core is working for agent harnesses: free MIT repo, paid shared credits, spending caps and a shared skills library. Caveat: clone and token-share figures are self-reported and enterprise customers are unnamed.
analysis.future: Watch revenue against the $100M target. A niche for builders: vertical skill packs on top of an open harness.

items.headline: AWS Open-Sources Strands Box, an Agent Sandbox That Enforces Rules on What the Agent Has Already Done
items.dek: Not just container isolation: a local policy engine that checks each tool call against the agent's own history.

analysis.happening: AWS announced Strands Box on Oct 7. It adds OS-level isolation plus the Dogwood Local Engine, which can cap actions over time, such as 3 Slack posts per 10 minutes. It works with any harness. macOS only today, Linux in development.
analysis.now: Agent safety is moving from 'run it in a VM' to policy over the action sequence, a template a solo builder can copy. Caveat: one report calls the Dogwood reference interpreter not production-ready, and bad outcomes remain possible.
analysis.future: Watch the Linux build, AgentCore/Kubernetes deployment, and whether Claude Code or Codex users adopt Dogwood-style policies.

items.headline: Rapidus Launches 'CORE' With 17 Design Partners, but Still Has No Named 2nm Customer
items.dek: Japan's state-backed foundry is building a design-support network before signing a single production order.

analysis.happening: On Oct 5 Rapidus unveiled Rapidus CORE with 17 firms including Synopsys, Cadence, Infosys, Dai Nippon Printing and Toppan. It plans 2nm output at its Hokkaido plant from April 2027 and runs test production with IBM. No customer order is named; state support is about $15B.
analysis.now: Gap versus TSMC: TSMC, Samsung and Intel already produce at this node, and prospects reportedly cannot move all work off TSMC. CORE shows Rapidus selling a design flow, not just wafers.
analysis.future: Watch for the first named 2nm customer and customer test chips by late 2026. Design-service firms around CORE are an opening for a builder.

items.headline: Fujitsu Opens Trials of Four Retail AI Agents With 7 Retailers, but General Availability Is Not Until June 2027
items.dek: Japan's enterprise AI arrives as vertical agents sold by incumbent IT vendors, on a slower rollout than US peers.

analysis.happening: On Oct 6 Fujitsu began offering trial environments for four retail agents (sales-structure analysis, loyalty analysis, merchandise planning, store-manager support) plus an execution platform. Pilots start with 7 retailers; the official launch under Uvance for Retail is June 2027.
analysis.now: An eight-month trial-to-launch window is slow next to US agent startups shipping continuously, though Fujitsu's distribution inside Japanese retail IT is strong. No customer metrics were disclosed.
analysis.future: Watch which retailers publish results and whether pricing appears. A startup could ship faster, narrower agents on the same retail data, where store operations are still labor-heavy.

items.headline: estie, a Commercial Real-Estate Data Platform With Embedded AI, Wins TSE Growth Listing Approval at About ¥16.6B
items.dek: A UTEC-backed data startup goes public with Mitsui Fudosan and Mitsubishi Estate as anchor investors and AI partners.

analysis.happening: TSE approved estie (658A) on Oct 1, with listing Nov 6 at an expected ¥1,070 per share (about ¥16.58B market cap). FY2025 revenue was about ¥2.08B, first-half FY2026 revenue rose 96.8% to about ¥1.75B, and it still posts losses. UTEC's fund holds 18.98%.
analysis.now: Gap: Japanese AI-adjacent exits are roughly $110M-scale, versus US AI IPOs in the billions. But selling proprietary data plus embedded AI engineers to incumbents is distinctly Japanese. Proceeds are modest, about ¥864M.
analysis.future: Watch the Oct 20 price range, bookbuilding Oct 21-27 and first-day trading on Nov 6, a read on whether Growth-market investors pay for vertical AI-and-data businesses.

items.headline: Tokyo's DriveX Raises About $1.15M for AI Factory Scheduling That Replaces Excel
items.dek: A tiny seed round shows what real Japanese AI funding looks like, and the unglamorous problem it targets.

analysis.happening: DriveX (Tokyo, founded Feb 2022, CEO Atsuhiro Nagata) announced an early-stage round of about $1.15M; Dealroom's headline says $950K and its sidebar $1.5M, so the figure is inconsistent. Its tool reads Excel, CSV and PDF orders, builds schedules and integrates with ERP and MES systems.
analysis.now: Gap: US AI funding is dominated by multi-hundred-million rounds; this is under $2M with no named VC. The opening is Japan's Excel-and-expertise manufacturing planning. Caveat: amount uncertain, product unproven at scale.
analysis.future: Watch for a named lead investor and customer logos, and for similar vertical-AI tools aimed at Japanese SMB manufacturers still living in spreadsheets.
